a1.label: 1. Reporting when something failed
a1.why: An incident report needs an exact time and date, not a vague phrase.

a2.label: 2. Asking a user for something
a2.why: 'Could you…?' is polite; a bare imperative or 'why didn't you' sounds blunt or accusing.

a3.label: 3. Summarising what the user told you
a3.why: Reported speech shifts the tense back: 'appears' becomes 'appeared' after 'she said'.

a4.label: 4. Naming an unconfirmed cause
a4.why: 'May' marks a possible cause; 'must' and 'will' claim more certainty than you have.

a5.label: 5. Committing to a timeframe
a5.why: A named deadline is a commitment; 'soon' and 'as soon as possible' promise nothing.

a6.label: 6. Explaining a delay to a non-technical reader
a6.why: Plain wording beats jargon: 'SKU mismatch' and 'NIC revision' mean nothing to that reader.

a7.label: 7. Recording an action in a report
a7.why: Reports use the passive for actions taken: 'were disabled' focuses on what happened.

a8.label: 8. Closing a message that needs action
a8.why: A clear close names the action and the deadline, so the reader knows what to do.
